organism.overview: Eunice aphroditois is a predatory polychaete annelid with large jaws and a documented role in rapid ambush predation. This dossier conservatively represents contact and bite risk without claiming a fully characterized venom composition.
naturalHistory: It is a marine polychaete that can remain concealed in sediment.
The animal uses a rapid jaw strike to capture prey.
Its large size and nocturnal behavior contribute to ambush predation.

deliveryMechanism.summary: A rapid jaw strike can injure prey or a contacting organism; toxin composition is not characterized in this dossier.
sequence: The worm remains concealed in sediment.
A target approaches within striking distance.
Jaws extend rapidly and contact the target.

habitats.name: Marine sediment and reef-associated substrate
habitats.summary: Lives concealed in marine sediment or reef-associated substrate.

ecologicalRoles.summary: Rapid jaw strikes support predation on nearby marine animals.

summaryPoints: This dossier limits claims to documented taxonomy and predatory jaw contact.
